inputs.passages: Article title, passage text, passage ID, and paragraph order only.
inputs.queries: Visible question text only for query time and relation interpretation.

dev_pilot.use: Debug extraction and interfaces before final freeze.

human_test_confirmation.use: Published human questions; prior inspected baseline outcomes; confirmation only.

dev_additional_calibration.use: Source calibration only. Excluded from validation before outcomes.

ranking.tie_break: passage_id, then source offset, then claim_id
ranking.fixed_order_exception: The prespecified latest-mentioned-year comparator reorders the common top20 lexical units.

contexts.overflow: Take common fixed source prefixes for atomic units; stop at the shared word budget.
contexts.reader_input: Same source text and temporal metadata format in every condition.
contexts.unit_definition: Atomic source excerpt with exact source character offsets. Uncovered source text remains fallback units. Never reject a whole passage solely because one extracted event fails.

methods.earliest_completion: Set every occurrence bound and accepted endpoint to its lower bound, then use exact direct replacement.
methods.midpoint_completion: Set every occurrence bound and accepted endpoint to its interval midpoint, then use exact direct replacement.
methods.latest_completion: Set every occurrence bound and accepted endpoint to its upper bound, then use exact direct replacement.
methods.interval_outer_control: Keep a claim when its start lower bound is at most query end, and query start is strictly below explicit end upper bound. Ignore replacement pairs.
methods.possible_support: Use the exact possible-support mask under the fixed product model and fixed replacement pairs.
methods.guaranteed_support: Use the exact guaranteed-support mask under the same model and pairs. Keep unparsed text under the common fallback policy, but never label it guaranteed.
methods.latest_mentioned_year_top20: Within the same top20 lexical source units, prefer the latest source-mentioned year at most the query last year. Preserve lexical ties.

time_semantics.query: Closed window read from visible question. A year means January 1 through December 31; a month means its first through last day.
time_semantics.occurrence_start: An unknown event start constrained to one stated year, month, day, or explicit start bound.
time_semantics.validity_duration: A stated validity period. Never reinterpret its two endpoints as uncertain event start bounds.
time_semantics.end: Half-open retirement boundary [start,end); shift through-date endpoints only under an explicit source parser rule.
time_semantics.unbounded_or_approximate: Retain as unresolved. Do not assign a made-up finite uncertainty width.
time_semantics.gate: Use identical source-supported directed replacement pairs for all methods. Generic different values do not establish replacement.
time_semantics.fallback: Unparsed questions use the common lexical order. Undated, unresolved, and rejected claims remain common fallback text.

slices.all_questions: Every retained question in the frozen track.
slices.temporal_extraction_active: At least one bounded extracted claim occurs in the fixed top20 lexical passages.
slices.uncertain_start_active: At least one bounded non-singleton occurrence start occurs in those passages.
slices.replacement_active: At least one accepted directed pair targets one of those claims.
slices.completion_sensitive: At least two completion methods return different claim contexts. Post hoc descriptive mechanism slice, not a separately selected benchmark.

inference_policy: A method may use only the shared extracted evidence, fixed ranking, visible query, and its stated temporal policy.
audit_policy: Independent source audit sees source spans and extraction only; it does not see method names, outcomes, or benchmark answers. Call it model audit unless actual human annotators supply labels.
interpretation: Benchmark anchors measure annotated source coverage. They do not establish semantic entailment. Annotation strings may be aliases, concurrent values, or sequential values.
freeze_policy: Before validation inference, save code and config hashes. Record any later changes as protocol amendments. Do not tune after validation or test outcomes.
